verification_report.summary:
The complete submitted supplement passes the sequential audit, conditional on the stated smooth STW existence and uniqueness theorem and the accepted standard elliptic inputs. The external input matches [STW17, Theorem 1.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1503.04491v2#page=4): gamma0 may be arbitrary Hermitian, gamma is Gauduchon, and u_ours=2pi u_STW converts both differential terms exactly. Connectedness is explicitly assumed here. No prerequisite proof uses this supplement circularly.

Differentiating eta^(n-1)=Gamma gives the stated n/(n-1) factor. The gradient term is first order, the principal symbol is positive definite, and the maximum principle gives the constant kernel. Index zero and Fredholm solvability give a one-dimensional smooth adjoint kernel; the nonzero-integral argument, nonnegative-test-function argument, and modified-adjoint strong minimum principle establish the unique strictly positive normalized density, including with drift.

Every integration-by-parts sign and the real-part factor 1/2 is correct. The terms involving A wedge partial barpartial K cancel, leaving precisely A_gamma(A). The n=2 specialization and A_gamma(gamma)=ddc(gamma^(n-1))/(n-1) are valid. The proof correctly distinguishes this adjoint equation from the Gauduchon condition on eta alone.

The positive cofactor map has a smooth inverse. The mean-normalized Holder-space derivative (v,a) maps to L_u v-a and has a bounded inverse with a=-integral h dmu, justifying the implicit-function argument without differentiating the supremum. The determinant identity det Q proportional to (det eta)^(n-1), frame invariance, and nonnegativity of the trace-square term justify both variation formulas, including the second-derivative factor 1/(n-1). Equality along an affine density family occurs exactly for a spatially constant direction. Translation, concavity, and the Lipschitz bound follow.

In dimension two with gamma0 Gauduchon, both additional terms in the integrated mass expansion vanish by Stokes. The stated log-partition formula, constant adjoint multiplier, Gibbs probability, and negative-variance second derivative follow. Uniform approximation gives the unique continuous scalar extension. No weak STW solution, BMP/PVP, or independent proof of the deep existence estimate is inferred. All 15 sequential checks and three reference/dependency checks passed; no critical errors or gaps were found. The manuscript was read without modification.
